messages:
incident-bot: :bell: ALERT: Elevated TLS handshake failures seen for hosted endpoints in us-west-2 starting ~18:04 UTC. Error spike: 12% of requests failing with TLS handshake errors (openssl: 'sslv3 alert certificate unknown' & 'unexpected eof while reading'). Pager: @oncall-sre. Incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/2061112222

maya: oncall ack. I'm in. quick summary: customers report intermittent 502/524 responses; internal metrics show handshake drop around 18:03. Starting timeline and evidence collection.

sre_raj: taking lead for SRE. @netops_sam @infra_lea can you join? Key asks: cert rollout logs, ELB/edge cert chain, route table changes, and packet captures.

netops_sam: joining. Quick checks: pulled cert currently served by edge LB in us-west-2:
```
# openssl x509 -in /tmp/edge_cert.pem -noout -subject -issuer -text | sed -n '1,8p'
subject=CN = redwood-edge-usw2
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
    DNS:edge-us-west.redwood.ai, DNS:canary.edge-us-west.redwood.ai
```
Edge cert looks valid but missing SAN for `api-us-west.redwood.ai` (our external hostname uses SNI to route). Rolling cert job ran at 17:50 UTC (deploy-pipeline/ci-rotations/2026-03-11).

infra_lea: I see the cert-rotation job applied a new bundle 17:49:58 UTC. The bundle mapping changed how SNI hostnames are mapped to certs (we recently consolidated names). Could be misconfiguration in rotation manifest. Dump from cert-rotation logs:
```
2026-03-11T17:49:58Z rotate-cert: bundle v12 applied to env=us-west-2
applied_mappings: ["edge-us-west.redwood.ai" => "/secrets/certs/v12.pem"]
```
No explicit mapping for `api-us-west.redwood.ai` due to a manifest mismatch.

sre_raj: that's a strong signal for a cert/SNI mismatch. But parallel traces show network-level icmp 'need to frag' in packets between ELB and backend nodes during same window. Running tcpdump now.

netops_sam: tcpdump snippet (redacted IPs):
```
18:03:11.001234 IP 10.200.3.1.443 > 10.200.10.77.51515: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 32768, length 1460
18:03:11.001235 IP 10.200.10.77 > 10.200.3.1: ICMP 10.200.3.1 unreachable - need to frag (mtu 1400)
18:03:11.001236 IP 10.200.10.77.51515 > 10.200.3.1.443: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```
Frequent ICMP need-to-frag. Path MTU looks off on peered path.

vendor_bot: FYI vendor alerting: peering appliance upgrade to 5.4.1 was auto-applied in us-west-2 at 03:00 UTC today. Release notes mention stricter DF handling for tunneled traffic. (ref: VNDR-2026-05).

infra_lea: cross-checking route changes: route CR-2026-0311 modified peering route table at 17:30 UTC (removed some legacy /24s). Noted. Could be unrelated but timeline overlaps.

maya: hypotheses: A) cert rotation dropped `api-*` SNI mapping => LB serves wrong cert -> client rejects handshake. B) PMTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello truncation -> handshake abort. C) Peering appliance firmare + route cleanup exposed PMTU mismatch. We'll gather evidence and pick mitigations.

sre_raj: evidence summary so far: cert rotation ran before the spike + edge cert bundle doesn't include the external API SAN -> supports hypothesis A. tcpdump shows ICMP need-to-frag -> supports B/C. Need to prioritize quick mitigations that restore customer traffic.

netops_sam: mitigation plan attempt 1: re-route traffic to fallback transit gateway (tg-ops) that does not traverse peering appliance (we can flip a route table for LB backends). Doing a canary route change for 2 subnets now.

infra_lea: also starting rollback of cert bundle mapping to previous manifest v11 for canaries. Command: `rotate-cert --env=us-west-2 --bundle=v11 --dry-run=false --canary-subnets=subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb` — executing now.

netops_sam: canary route flip done. Re-running curl test to problematic endpoint from external test-runner:
```
# before route flip: openssl s_client -connect api-us-west.redwood.ai:443 -servername api-us-west.redwood.ai
CONNECTED(00000003)
140348123456792:error:140770FC:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol:s23_clnt.c:???
# after route flip:
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
POST /health 200 OK
```
Canary shows success after route flip. Error rates on those subnets dropped from 11% -> 0.8%.

infra_lea: cert rollback to v11 applied to those canaries as well. Checking `openssl s_client` servercert now shows SAN includes `api-us-west.redwood.ai`.

sre_raj: both mitigations together improved success. Which one was primary? We need to disambiguate. netops, can you re-run tcpdump across both path variants and see if ICMP need-to-frag persists on the original peered path?

netops_sam: tcpdump on original path still shows ICMP need-to-frag and some resets. On transit-gw path (the fallback) no ICMP need-to-frag. So stepping back: two independent problems: cert mapping caused many connections to fail early, and PMTU mismatch on peering path caused additional handshake truncation. The route flip avoided PMTU problem for now.

pm_sasha: drafting customer comms: will note service disruption and interim mitigations (route reroute + cert rollback) and that a postmortem will follow.

infra_lea: owners and next steps:
- infra_lea: roll full cert manifest rollback if we can't validate corrected manifest; investigate manifest bug in rotation pipeline (owner: infra_lea)
- netops_sam: schedule controlled maintenance to test peering appliance firmware rollback or MTU reconciliation with vendor; keep transit-gw route as long-term fallback until we fix underlying path (owner: netops_sam)
- sre_raj: lead RCA write-up, timeline, and attach tcpdumps/logs (owner: sre_raj)

netops_sam: timeline updates: 18:03 UTC spike; 18:07 UTC canary route flip -> immediate improvement; 18:09 UTC cert rollback on canaries -> further reduction. 18:20 UTC rolled route flip to all LB backends, cert rollback staged for full env after manifest fix. Error rates back to baseline ~0.6% at 18:30.

sre_raj: tagging follow-ups for root cause: 1) rotation manifest validation gap (missing SAN mapping) 2) vendor appliance firmware change + route cleanup revealed PMTU mismatch. Proposed remediations: add manifest schema validation + preflight that verifies SNI->cert mappings, add path MTU monitoring and CI tests for peering paths, and coordinate with vendor to test firmware or adjust MTU on tunnel.

maya: capturing artifacts: cert-rotation logs, previous bundle v11 and v12 diffs, tcpdumps from peered path and transit-gw path, ELB logs with handshake errors, route-change CRs. Attaching to incident doc.

infra_lea: we'll also add a pre-rotation smoke test that does `openssl s_client -connect ... -servername ...` across real hostnames in each AZ and fail the rotation if any mapping missing.

pm_sasha: published initial customer update at 18:35 UTC: "We observed TLS handshake errors affecting requests in us-west-2. We routed traffic to an alternative transit path and rolled back a recent certificate bundle for canaries; full mitigations applied. We will publish a postmortem."

incident-bot: Incident 2061112222 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: reduced. Postmortem required.

sre_raj: passing to next oncall for monitoring. I'll own the RCA write-up. Handoff ack to @maya.

maya: accepted handoff. I'll coordinate the vendor window and the rotation pipeline fix. Thanks team. :handshake:
